Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant transition you're going through as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling during this postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource for us to better understand your emotional well-being right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and held in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and provide guidance without judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us gain insight into your feelings and experiences over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and natural as possible.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be able to laugh and joke around with my friends and family, but since having the baby, it feels like that part of me has kind of... faded away. I do try to watch funny videos or TV shows, but they just don't seem as funny as they used to. And when my husband or friends try to make me laugh, I might smile for a second, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. It's like, I can see that something is supposed to be funny, but I just can't seem to connect with it on a deeper level. Some days are better than others, but overall, I'd say I've only really laughed a few times in the past week, and it's always been a pretty weak laugh. It's just hard for me to feel like my old self when I'm so tired and worried all the time... (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really frustrating for me to feel like I've lost that part of myself.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I don't think I have, not really. Like I said, I've tried to watch funny things and my husband has tried to make me laugh, but it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. The baby is always crying, or I'm worried that she's not eating enough, or I'm just so tired... it's hard to find the energy to laugh or see the humor in things. Sometimes I'll be playing with the baby and she'll do something cute, and for a second, I'll feel a little spark of happiness, but it's not the same as really laughing or feeling carefree. It's like, I'm just trying to survive most of the time, you know? (sighs) I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and it's really sad for me because I used to be a pretty happy, carefree person.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like so much work. Even simple things, like taking a shower or going for a walk, feel like huge tasks. And when I do try to plan something, like a visit with friends or a trip to the store, I just end up feeling anxious about how it will all work out with the baby. Will she cry the whole time? Will I be able to get everything done that I need to? It's just so overwhelming. 

I do try to look forward to things, like my husband coming home from work or a visit from my mom, but even those things can feel stressful because I worry about whether the baby will be fussy or if I'll be able to get everything done that I need to. And sometimes, even when I do have something to look forward to, I just feel so tired and drained that I don't even have the energy to enjoy it. It's like, I'll be thinking about something fun that's going to happen, but then I'll just start feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and it takes all the joy out of it. (sighs) It's hard to explain, but it just feels like everything is so much harder now, and it's taking a toll on my ability to enjoy things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... all the time. I feel like I'm just not doing anything right. If the baby cries, I think it's because I'm not feeding her properly or I'm not changing her diaper fast enough. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough or I'm not taking care of myself. I just feel like I'm constantly making mistakes and that I'm not good enough to be a mother. 

Even when my husband tries to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm failing somehow. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to buy diapers or if I don't have a chance to wash the baby's clothes, I feel like I'm a terrible mother. It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong so that I can beat myself up over it. 

It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm always walking on eggshells, waiting for the other shoe to drop. And when things do go wrong, I just feel like it's all my fault. I don't know how to stop feeling this way, it's just like my mind is constantly criticizing me and telling me that I'm not good enough. (starts to tear up) It's really hard to deal with, and it makes me feel so alone and so guilty all the time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I worry about everything. I worry that the baby is going to get sick, or that she's not eating enough, or that she's not developing fast enough. I worry that I'm not doing enough for her, or that I'm doing too much and smothering her. I worry that my husband is going to get tired of helping me with the baby and leave me. I worry that I'm going to mess up the baby's schedule, or that I'm going to forget something important.

It's like, my mind is just constantly racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I don't know how to turn it off. Even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I still find myself worrying about something. It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? 

And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to sleep, my mind just starts racing with all these worries and fears. I'll be lying there, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I just can't seem to calm myself down. It's like, my brain is just wired to worry, and I don't know how to stop it.

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me, and he'll be like, "Everything is fine, the baby is healthy, you're doing a great job." But even when he says that, I just can't seem to shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. It's like, I'm just stuck in this cycle of worry and anxiety, and I don't know how to get out of it. (sighs) It's really exhausting, to be honest.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no reason for it. The baby is fine, everything is okay, but I just can't seem to calm down.

It's really scary, to be honest. I'll be thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling this way?" And I'll try to take deep breaths and calm myself down, but it's hard. Sometimes, I'll even start to cry, and I'll feel like I'm losing control.

It's not just when I'm alone with the baby, either. Sometimes, it'll happen when my husband is home, or when we're out in public. I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of anxiety, and I'll start to panic. It's like, my body is just on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He'll be like, "What's wrong? Is everything okay?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel really scared and panicked." And he'll try to reassure me, but it's hard to shake the feeling.

It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? And even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I still can't seem to shake this feeling of impending doom. It's really hard to deal with, and it's affecting my daily life. I just feel like I'm walking around on edge all the time, waiting for something to happen. (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I feel. It's like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and it's exhausting. I mean, I love her to death, but it's just so much work. And on top of that, I'm trying to manage the house, and cook meals, and do laundry... it's just never-ending.

And it's not just the physical stuff, either. It's the emotional stuff, too. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right. And if I'm not worrying about the baby, I'm worrying about myself, and whether I'm losing my identity as a person. It's like, I'm just getting lost in all of this, and I don't know how to find my way back.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling completely overwhelmed, and I'll just start to cry. I'll be like, "I don't know how to do this. I don't know how to be a good mom. I don't know how to keep up with all of this." And my husband will try to reassure me, but it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough.

It's like, everything is just getting on top of me, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. I feel like I'm drowning in all of this responsibility, and I don't know how to stay afloat. (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about. I feel like I'm just failing at everything, and it's really scary.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's me. I've been having a really hard time sleeping. I'll be lying in bed, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries. I'll be thinking about the baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right. And if I'm not thinking about the baby, I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, and how I'm going to get everything done.

And even when I'm not thinking about all those things, I'll just feel this... this sadness, I guess. It's like, a weight is just pressing down on me, and I don't know how to lift it. I'll be lying there, feeling so unhappy and so overwhelmed, and I just won't be able to sleep.

Sometimes, I'll be awake for hours, just lying there and staring at the ceiling. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these... these anxious dreams, I guess. I'll be dreaming about the baby, and something will be wrong, and I'll wake up feeling just as anxious and overwhelmed as I did when I went to bed.

It's like, I'm just not able to relax, you know? I'm always on edge, always waiting for something to go wrong. And it's affecting my sleep, and it's affecting my mood, and it's just... it's really hard to deal with.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive. He'll try to help me relax, and he'll listen to me when I'm feeling anxious and overwhelmed. But even with his help, it's just... it's hard to shake this feeling of unhappiness and anxiety. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the background, waiting to pounce. (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's me. I've been feeling really sad and miserable a lot of the time. It's like, this heaviness is just weighing me down, and I don't know how to lift it. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start to cry. I'll be thinking about how much I love her, and how much I want to be a good mom, but I'll just feel so overwhelmed and sad.

It's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be with my husband, or with friends, and I'll just start to feel this... this sadness, I guess. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the background, waiting to pounce. And sometimes, it'll just hit me out of nowhere. I'll be doing okay, and then suddenly, I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive. He'll listen to me, and he'll try to reassure me, but it's hard to shake this feeling of sadness. It's like, it's just a part of me now, and I don't know how to get rid of it.

Sometimes, I'll be feeling okay, and then I'll think about all the things I need to do, or all the things that could go wrong, and it'll just trigger this... this sadness, I guess. It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? And it's hard to enjoy the present moment, because I'm always worrying about the future.

I feel like I've lost myself, too. I used to be a happy person, I used to be able to find joy in things, but now it's just... it's hard. Everything feels like a struggle, and I just feel so sad and miserable all the time. (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about. I feel like I'm just failing at everything, and it's really scary.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to cry. Sometimes, it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes, it's just because I'm feeling so sad and miserable.

I've been crying a lot at night, too. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll just start to think about everything, and I'll start to cry. I'll be thinking about the baby, and how much I love her, but also how much I'm struggling to take care of her. And I'll be thinking about my husband, and how much I appreciate him, but also how much I feel like I'm burdening him with all my emotions.

Sometimes, I'll be crying, and my husband will try to comfort me, but it's hard to stop once I've started. It's like, once the tears start flowing, it's like a dam has burst, and I just can't stop crying. And sometimes, I'll be crying, and the baby will start to cry, too, and it's just... it's really hard.

I feel like I'm just so emotional all the time, and it's hard to control my emotions. I'll be feeling okay, and then suddenly, I'll just start to cry. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I'll be out in public, or with friends, and I'll just start to feel this... this sadness, I guess, and I'll start to cry.

It's like, I'm just so unhappy, and I don't know how to be happy again. I feel like I've lost myself, and I don't know how to find my way back. And the crying, it's just... it's like my body's way of releasing all the emotions that I've been holding inside. (starts to tear up) Sorry, it's just really hard to talk about. I feel like I'm just falling apart, and I don't know how to put the pieces back together again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think so. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through all of this, but I don't think I've ever thought about harming myself. I've just felt like I'm not doing a good enough job, and that I'm just trying to survive each day, but I don't think I've ever had any thoughts of self-harm.

I think I've just felt really frustrated and sad, and I've wondered if I'm cut out for this whole motherhood thing, but I don't think I've ever had any thoughts of hurting myself. I've just felt like I'm trying to do my best, and that I'm just taking things one day at a time.

I've had some really tough moments, though. I've felt like I'm just not good enough, and that I'm just pretending to be a mom. But I don't think I've ever had any thoughts of self-harm. I think I've just felt really scared and alone, and like I'm just trying to figure everything out.

I'm glad you asked me that, though. It's nice to know that you're checking in with me, and that you care about how I'm feeling. It's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff, but it's nice to know that I can be honest with you.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient presents with several symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. Main symptoms expressed include persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells. The patient reports difficulty finding joy in activities, feeling overwhelmed, and experiencing anxiety and panic.

Consistent patterns across answers include low mood, loss of enjoyment, anxiety, guilt, and difficulty coping with the responsibilities of motherhood. The patient expresses feelings of worthlessness and guilt, particularly in regards to her ability to care for her baby.

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression or anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Difficulty coping with the responsibilities of motherhood

Specific risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety and panic
* Overwhelming feelings of responsibility and self-doubt

Notably, the patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation.

**Screening Observation Summary:**
The patient's responses suggest a high risk for postpartum depression and/or anxiety. The patient's symptoms, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, are consistent with postpartum depression. The patient's feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and difficulty coping with the responsibilities of motherhood also raise concerns. Further evaluation and assessment are recommended to determine the presence and severity of postpartum depression and/or anxiety.
